author: Inside Edition
description: While driving through a Mississippi storm, a man's car was struck by lightning. It happened near Tylertown as storm chaser Aaron Rigsby was driving 55 miles an hour. Still shaken, Rigsby realized he had a new problem, his car was fried. Calling a fellow storm chaser on his radio, Rigsby pulled off the road. He grabbed his camera from the stalled vehicle and got out of there. He still had a tornado to chase. He spoke with Inside Edition's Alison Hall.
title: Storm Chaser's Car Struck By Lightning While Driving

author: Inside Edition
description: Authorities said a former supermarket employee showed up at the supermarket and pointed a gun at a security guard in the parking lot. It triggered an immediate lockdown. Blogger Raya Hensler was one of about 40 shoppers ushered into the stockroom of an H-E-B store in Houston, Texas. Hensler spoke with Inside Edition. Eventually the police sounded the all-clear. Cops say the man with the gun was fired five years ago, but has regularly returned to the store harassing employees.
title: Supermarket Goes On Lockdown After Former Employee Allegedly Shows Up With Gun

author: Inside Edition
description: A woman out walking alone was suddenly confronted by a pack of wild dogs. The dogs pounced on 65-year-old Dorrie Reyes, leaving most of her body ripped and torn. Inside Edition spoke to her daughter Rhenell Schiller. She says there were so many bites on her mother's body that doctors stopped counting. Reyes was saved by good Samaritans, a husband and wife who heard her cries for help. A police department spokesperson says three of the dogs were captured and there is an ongoing effort to locate and capture the others.
title: 65-Year-Old Woman Suffers Serious Injuries After Being Attacked By Pack Of Wild Dogs

author: Inside Edition
description: Countries around the world are trying to prevent another pandemic after an outbreak of hantavirus on a cruise ship killed three people. Officials in Argentina, where the ship departed en route to Antarctica, are trying to find out if it is the source of the outbreak. The World Health Organization says the country consistently has the most reported cases of the rare disease in Latin America. Inside Edition Digital’s Mara Montalbano has more.
title: The Worldwide Effort To Contain The Hantavirus
